title: Host Damage Protection (HostCover) Terms: Payment of Claims
content:
Roamhaven pays a **Host Damage Protection (HostCover)** claim only on the conditions of this section. Passages withdrawn from the section are marked no longer in force where they stand.

## Conditions of payment (in force)

1. Roamhaven pays a claim only after the guest has not paid it in full.
2. A reimbursement is paid only on a claim the claims team has approved.
3. A claim is escalated to Roamhaven only after the guest's response deadline has passed or the guest has declined, and the host must escalate within the level's escalation window in calendar days after the guest's response deadline (30 calendar days on every level). The deadline is the request time plus the level's guest response time (72 hours on every level), and the days are counted from the date part of that deadline, an escalation on the last day standing.
4. The stay must have checked in on or after the plan's effective date while the plan was active.
5. A payable amount of 0.00 is recorded as a denial, not a payment.
6. A claim is reimbursed once.
7. The reimbursement is credited to the default payout method.

## Payable amount

The clause on the payable amount reads as follows, withdrawn passages marked:

- "The payable amount is computed in this order: start from the verified loss;" **no longer in force.**
- "for property-damage, pet-damage, theft and valuables claims, when the level pays items at depreciated value, deduct the depreciation-schedule percentage for the item's age in whole months (0 to 12, 13 to 36, 37 to 60, 61 and over);" **no longer in force.**
- For a deep-cleaning claim, when the level reduces deep-cleaning claims by the cleaning fee, deduct the cleaning fee collected on the stay. *In force.*
- "subtract every guest payment recorded on the claim (net of reversals)" **no longer in force.**
- "subtract the level's deductible" **no longer in force.**
- Floor at 0.00; then cut to the category's sublimit (the pet-damage, deep-cleaning, theft or valuables sublimit; property damage and income loss have none), to the per-claim limit, and to the remaining aggregate of the plan year. *In force.*

On income loss: an income-loss claim is covered only where the level covers lost income, and it takes no depreciation (*in force*); the passage "its verified loss is the nightly subtotal of the stays the host had to cancel for at most the level's maximum nights" is **no longer in force**.

Each passage marked no longer in force has been superseded by the current settlement terms for the kind of claim concerned.

## Escalation window, case by case (hypothetical)

| Payment request sent | Guest response deadline | Date part of deadline | Escalated on | Days after deadline date | Within the window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-02 at 15:00 | 2026-06-05 at 15:00 | 2026-06-05 | 2026-07-05 | 30 | Yes, the last day |
| 2026-06-02 at 15:00 | 2026-06-05 at 15:00 | 2026-06-05 | 2026-07-06 | 31 | No |

An escalation is possible only once the deadline has passed or the guest has declined; a guest who declines on 3 June opens escalation before 5 June, and the 30 days are still counted from the date part of the deadline.

superseded_clauses: The payable amount is computed in this order: start from the verified loss;

for property_damage, pet_damage, theft and valuables claims, when depreciation_applies is true, deduct the depreciation_schedule percentage for the item's age in whole months (0-12, 13-36, 37-60, 61 and over);
subtract every guest payment recorded on the claim (net of reversals)
its verified loss is the nightly subtotal of the stays the host had to cancel for at most income_loss_max_nights nights
